lessons.expressionTask: Tom and Lily talk about their family. What do they say?

context: Tom and Lily talk about their family.
Tom says, 'We are a close-knit family. Three generations live in our house.'
dialogue: Tom, is your family big?
Yes. We are an extended family. Three generations live in our house.
What is a generation?
It is people born at about the same time.
Do you have a family tree?
Yes. We made a family tree at school. My uncle is a blood relative.

lessons.question: How many generations live in Tom's house?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Tom and Lily talk about their family. Tom says, 'We are a close-knit family. Three generations live in our house. My mother, my father, my brother and my sister live with me, and my grandparents live with us too.' Lily says, 'What is a generation?' Tom says, 'It is people born at about the same time. My grandparents, my parents and I are three generations.' Lily says, 'Is your family big?' Tom says, 'Yes. We are an extended family. We made a family tree at school. My uncle is a blood relative, and my aunt is a blood relative too.' Lily says, 'Good. I can talk about my family.'

Tom says, 'I get on well with my sister. My stepbrother is older than me.'
dialogue: Lily, do you get on well with your sister?
Yes. I get on well with my sister. We play together.
Do you have a stepbrother?
Yes. My stepbrother is older than me. He plays the piano.
Do brothers and sisters fall out with each other?
Sometimes. Sometimes brothers fall out with each other, but they can drift apart or stay close.

Lily says, 'Do brothers and sisters fall out with each other?' Tom says, 'Sometimes brothers fall out with each other. They can drift apart over the years, but my family talks a lot.
